rendered.overview: [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] leads a five-color Ally pile built around triggering waterbend, earthbend, firebend, and airbend to draw cards and flip into a card-draw, damage-dealing threat. Alongside this, [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and the commander can loop infinite creature ETB and LTB triggers, making infinite tokens and storm count.

strategy: Ramp out mana to cast [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Trigger all four bending types in a turn to draw cards and flip the commander.
Assemble [[Aang, the Last Airbender]], [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]], and the commander to loop infinite tokens.
Use Lesson spells to fuel [[Gran-Gran]] and [[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] for value and land creatures.
Close games with flipped commander damage or an army of Ally tokens.

keep: Keeping lands that fix all five colors sets up the commander.
sendBack: A hand with no way to produce more than one color struggles here.

tips.text: [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] airbending [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] recasts it cheaply to retrigger its enter effect.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] earthbends extra counters when you cast Lesson spells like [[Waterbending Lesson]].
[[Gran-Gran]] loots whenever tapped, filling the graveyard to power [[Accumulate Wisdom]].

rendered.overview: [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] leads a colorless deck built around casting huge spells that trigger double cascade, chaining into more colorless spells for value and board control. The deck ramps hard with artifacts like [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Thran Dynamo]], then floods the board with Eldrazi and constructs while [[Forsaken Monument]] and [[Basalt Monolith]] together can make infinite colorless mana.

rendered.overview: This Naya deck leads with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]], flooding the board with Dinosaurs off combat damage, while enrage triggers from creatures like [[Polyraptor]] and [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] push toward repeatable value or infinite loops with [[Walking Ballista]], [[Forerunner of the Empire]], or [[Marauding Raptor]]. The deck grinds with card advantage engines and finishes through overwhelming Dinosaur combat or an assembled combo loop.

strategy: Ramp early with pieces like [[Topiary Stomper]] and [[Ranging Raptors]] toward casting [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]].
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to put free Dinosaurs onto the battlefield from the top of your library.
Trigger enrage payoffs such as [[Polyraptor]] and [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] to flood the board with tokens and counters.
Assemble [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]] for infinite tokens and damage, or [[Marauding Raptor]] with [[Polyraptor]] to draw the game.
Use [[Walking Ballista]] alongside [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] to generate infinite +1/+1 counters without spending mana.

keep: A hand with [[Ranging Raptors]] and early lands can ramp into your game plan.
sendBack: A hand with no way to fix Naya colors risks stumbling on early plays.
A hand heavy on expensive Dinosaurs but no ramp stalls before casting them.

tips.text: Use [[Boxing Ring]] to trigger fights whenever a creature you control enters, feeding [[Bellowing Aegisaur]]'s enrage.
Cast [[Marauding Raptor]] before [[Polyraptor]] so creature triggers can loop damage into infinite tokens.

Enrage makes token copies, core combo payoff piece.
Finds Dinosaurs and loops damage with Polyraptor.
Cost reducer that chains creature ETB damage into loops.

Moderate: Without [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] connecting, the deck loses its main way to cheat Dinosaurs like [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]] into play.

rendered.overview: This mono-red Goblin tribal deck leads with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] turning a board of Goblins into an exploding army, then converts the swarm into damage through sacrifice outlets and burn spells. With [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] alongside [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]], the deck can chain infinite commander casts and infinite hasty Goblin tokens for the win. Even without the combo, a wide Goblin board plus haste enablers closes games through combat damage or direct burn.

strategy: Ramp early with artifacts and Goblins to get [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] out around turn 4.
Tap [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] to flood the board with 1/1 Goblin tokens each turn it survives.
Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite tokens and casts.
Give the token army haste via [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Bloodlust Inciter]] to attack the same turn.
Finish with burn spells like [[Fireball]] or sacrifice outlets such as [[Goblin Bombardment]] if combat is blocked.

keep: [[Skirk Prospector]] early lets Goblins fuel extra mana and future casts.
A hand with ramp like [[Sol Ring]] into a turn 4 commander plan is solid.
sendBack: A hand with no red sources to reliably cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] is risky.
Too many expensive spells and no Goblins to protect [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] is weak.

tips.text: Sacrifice a Goblin to [[Skirk Prospector]] to pay for more spells, then recur mana with [[Goblin Lookout]] pumping the rest.
Use [[Goblin Bombardment]] to sacrifice extra tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for direct damage.
Enchant a creature with [[Dragon Breath]] to give it haste, then pump it with [[Crown of Fury]] for first strike.

weaknesses: Critical: Removing [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] before it taps breaks the infinite combo with [[Goblin Warchief]] and [[Skirk Prospector]].
Moderate: Without [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] on board the token engine stalls and the deck loses its main payoff.
Minor: The deck leans on artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] but has only a few answers if opponents remove them.

Draw and burn with [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] off stored experience counters.
Chain extra combats with [[Aggravated Assault]] or [[World at War]] for lethal swings.

keep: A hand with [[Smothering Tithe]] and lands keeps mana flowing.
sendBack: A hand missing red or white sources can't reliably cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]].
A hand with no early plays before turn 4 stalls your plan.

tips.text: Attack with [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] then dump counters via [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] onto it for burn triggers.
[[Otharri, Suns' Glory]] attacks make Rebel tokens that can also carry [[Kratos, Stoic Father]]'s end step counters.
[[Ilharg, the Raze-Boar]] attacking with Gods helps trigger [[Kratos, Stoic Father]]'s experience gain.

rendered.overview: [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] leads a ninja tribal plan built around slipping unblockable attackers through combat and ninjutsu-swapping them for bigger ninjas to trigger life loss and card advantage. Cheap evasive creatures like [[Slither Blade]] and [[Tormented Soul]] attack, get bounced into [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] or other ninjas, and each hit drains life equal to a revealed card's mana value while digging cards. Backed by counterspells and cheap removal, the deck grinds down life totals through repeated combat damage rather than big single swings.

keyCards.job: Converts combat damage into life loss and cards.
Grants ninjutsu to every creature card in hand.
Reanimates an opposing creature on hit.
Finds another Ninja card after connecting.
Generates Treasure off ninja damage.
Lets you cast an opponent's exiled cards free.
Draws a card off unblocked combat damage.

weaknesses: Moderate: The deck has no answer to an opposing artifact or enchantment like a resolved [[Cursed Totem]].
Moderate: Without [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] connecting, the life-loss engine stops and the deck leans on ninjas alone.
Moderate: The plan relies almost entirely on unblocked combat damage, so a card like [[Ghostly Prison]] can stall it out.
